record.paper_title: Open Problems within Nonextensive Statistical Mechanics
record.original_question: Within Nonextensive Statistical Mechanics (NSM), should the generalized exponential function be applied to the survival function rather than to the probability density function when defining the generalized algebra of NSM? If the survival function is the more natural object to generalize, should the shape parameter, rather than the parameter q, become the fundamental parameter of the NSM generalization of statistical mechanics, especially because for nonzero coupling the reciprocal of the exponential function, rather than negating its argument, is what matters in defining distributions?

evidence.quote: This leads to a question regarding the definitions for the generalized algebra of NSM. In the development of NSM, the generalization of the exponential function has been applied to the pdf; however , would the sf be the more natural function to generalize? If so, then the shape parameter rather than q becomes the fundamental parameter of the NSM generalization of statistical mechanics.

A related issue is that exp4(−𝑧)≠exp4+'(𝑧) for 𝜅≠0. This is important in the definition of distributions since it’s the reciprocal of the exponential function rather than the negative of the argument that is important.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. In nonextensive statistical mechanics one replaces the ordinary exponential function by a one-parameter deformation. Two standard families are:

(i) Tsallis q-exponential: for a real parameter q,
   exp_q(x) := [1 + (1−q) x]_+^{1/(1−q)},  with exp_1(x) = e^x.

(ii) Kaniadakis κ-exponential: for a real shape parameter κ,
   exp_κ(x) := ( κ x + sqrt(1 + κ^2 x^2) )^{1/κ},  with exp_0(x) = e^x.

Given a nonnegative real-valued random variable X with probability density function (pdf) f(x) and survival function (sf) S(x) = Pr(X > x) = ∫_x^∞ f(t) dt, the construction of deformed (nonextensive) distributions is traditionally carried out by applying a generalized exponential directly to the pdf, e.g. f(x) ∝ exp_q(−β H(x)) for some "energy" H, thereby treating q (or κ) as a fundamental parameter of the generalized statistical mechanics.

An alternative construction would apply the generalized exponential to the survival function instead: S(x) = exp_κ(−Λ(x)) for some cumulative hazard Λ(x), and derive the pdf as f(x) = −S'(x).

Question. Consider these two alternative foundations for the generalized algebra of nonextensive statistical mechanics:

(a) Is the survival function S, rather than the pdf f, the more natural object to which a generalized exponential should be applied when defining the deformed algebra and the associated families of distributions?

(b) If (a) is affirmed, should the shape parameter (e.g. the κ of the Kaniadakis deformation) replace q as the fundamental deformation parameter underlying the generalized statistical mechanics?

(c) Taking account of the fact that, for the Kaniadakis deformation, exp_κ(−z) ≠ 1/exp_κ(z) whenever κ ≠ 0 (so that "negating the argument" and "taking the reciprocal" are genuinely distinct operations on the deformed exponential), determine which of these two operations is the correct one to use in defining survival functions and equilibrium-type distributions in the generalized framework, and reconcile this choice with the algebraic identities required for a consistent generalized exponential/logarithm calculus.

Provide a definitive resolution: identify the natural primitive object (pdf vs. sf), the fundamental deformation parameter, and the correct algebraic conventions, and justify the choice from first principles of the deformed algebra and probability theory.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open conceptual problem in the foundations of nonextensive statistical mechanics. No published resolution was located; the matter remains a subject of ongoing discussion regarding whether to deform the pdf or the survival function and whether q or the shape parameter κ should be regarded as fundamental.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems within Nonextensive Statistical Mechanics
status_evidence.snippet: Lists foundational open questions including whether the generalized exponential should be applied to the survival function rather than the pdf.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly identified as open.
